title.en: Beijing: The Capital & Its Central Axis
title.zh: 北京：祖国的首都与中轴线

clips.send: Wanning Bridge. The oldest bridge on the axis (1285). First built in 1285 in the Yuan dynasty, and still used by traffic today. In Yuan times, grain boats on the Grand Canal passed under it into Jishuitan lake (today’s Shichahai), the canal’s northern end. Stone water creatures carved on its banks once watched the water level.

clips.send: Tian’anmen. Gate of Heavenly Peace. Built in 1417 as the front gate of the Imperial City, and given the name Tian’anmen in 1651. On 1 October 1949 the founding ceremony of the People’s Republic of China was held here. It appears on China’s national emblem.

clips.send: Tsinghua University. Today: Haidian, Beijing. One of China’s top universities, famous for engineering and science, next door to Peking University in northwest Beijing.

clips.send: Festooned gate (垂花门). The “second gate”. A beautifully carved gate between the front yard and the inner courtyard; its painted wooden “flower” pendants hang down from the eaves. A saying about well-brought-up daughters: “never out the main gate, never past the second gate” (大门不出, 二门不迈).

clips.send: East wing (东厢房). Faces west. Bedrooms for the younger generation; traditionally the eldest son’s family lived in the east wing. It gets the afternoon sun.

clips.send: Main gate (大门). In the southeast corner. The gate is in a corner, not in the middle. Combined with the screen wall right inside, people in the hutong cannot look straight into the yard. It also cuts down the street wind and dust blowing in.

clips.send: Shichahai (Jishuitan). Today: Xicheng, Beijing. In the Yuan this lake, then called Jishuitan, was a busy harbour full of canal boats. Today people row boats in summer and skate on it in winter.

clips.send: Screen wall (影壁). Blocks the view from the gate. A decorated wall just inside (or opposite) the gate. Visitors turn left into the front yard, so the inside stays private and calm.

clips.send: Tian’anmen. On 1 October 1949 Chairman Mao Zedong stood on this gate tower and proclaimed the founding of the People’s Republic of China. The square in front can hold about a million people.

clips.send: Zhongguancun. Today: Haidian, Beijing. Called “China’s Silicon Valley”: thousands of tech companies sit next to famous universities and research institutes.

clips.send: The Forbidden City (Palace Museum). Home of 24 Ming and Qing emperors. Built 1406–1420. About 961 m long and 753 m wide ( about 72 hectares, about 135 football fields), ringed by a 10 m wall and a wide moat. About 8,700 rooms (counted in 间 jiān, the space between four pillars). The Hall of Supreme Harmony on the axis is China’s largest surviving wooden hall. You go in through the Meridian Gate (午门) in the south and out through the Gate of Divine Prowess (神武门) in the north. It became the Palace Museum in 1925 and a World Heritage Site in 1987.

It became the Palace Museum in 1925 and a World Heritage Site in 1987.

clips.send: Zhengyangmen (Qianmen). Main south gate of the inner city. Built in 1419. Its gate tower is about 43 m (141 ft) tall, the tallest of old Beijing’s city gates. In front stands an arrow tower with rows of small windows, built for archers to defend the gate. Outside it, Qianmen Street has been a busy shopping street for centuries.

clips.send: Main hall (正房). North side, facing south. The biggest, tallest building, for the grandparents or the head of the family. It faces south, so the low winter sun shines deep inside, while its wide eaves block the high summer sun. Its solid back wall faces north, into the cold winter wind.

clips.send: Temple of Heaven. Where emperors prayed for good harvests. Built in 1420 for the Ming and Qing emperors to worship heaven and pray for good harvests. World Heritage Site since 1998. The round Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests has three blue roofs: blue for the sky. It is about 38 m (125 ft) tall. The park wall is round in the north and square in the south: “round heaven, square earth” (天圆地方).

clips.send: Common mix-up: On a north-up map the Ancestral Temple is on the RIGHT (east), because “left” means the emperor’s left as he faces south.

clips.send: Huairou Science City. Today: Huairou, Beijing. A new science town in Beijing’s northern hills, home to big research facilities such as a high-energy light source.

clips.send: Side rooms (耳房). Small rooms beside the main hall. Lower and smaller, like “ears” on either side of the main hall. Used for storage, a kitchen or a study.

clips.send: Jingshan. A man-made hill with the best view. Piled up in the Ming dynasty, largely from the earth dug out for the palace moat. About 45 m (150 ft) high. The Wanchun Pavilion on top sits exactly on the axis. From the top you can see the golden roofs of the Forbidden City to the south and the Drum Tower to the north.

clips.send: Monument to the People’s Heroes. Today: Tian’anmen Square, Beijing. A 38 m granite obelisk on the Central Axis, honouring the people who gave their lives for China’s independence and liberation.
clips.text: Monument to the People’s Heroes. Today: Tian’anmen Square, Beijing. A 38 m granite obelisk on the Central Axis, honouring the people who gave their lives for China’s independence and liberation.

clips.send: Xiannongtan (Altar of Agriculture). West of the axis. Built in 1420. Each spring the emperor came here to plough a small field himself, to show how important farming was. It sits to the west of the axis, balancing the Temple of Heaven to the east. Today it houses the Beijing Ancient Architecture Museum.

clips.send: National Museum of China. Today: East side of Tian’anmen Square, Beijing. One of the biggest museums in the world, with more than a million objects — from Neolithic pottery and the Houmuwu ding to treasures of every dynasty.
clips.text: National Museum of China. Today: East side of Tian’anmen Square, Beijing. One of the biggest museums in the world, with more than a million objects — from Neolithic pottery and the Houmuwu ding to treasures of every dynasty.

clips.send: Drum Tower. Telling the time at night. First built in 1272 (Yuan), rebuilt in the Ming dynasty. About 47 m (154 ft) tall. Drums were beaten to mark the hours of the night: “morning bell, evening drum” (晨钟暮鼓). It once held 25 drums: one huge drum and 24 smaller ones, one for each of the 24 solar terms.

clips.send: Ancestral Temple and Altar of Land and Grain. “Temple on the left, altar on the right”. East of the axis: the Imperial Ancestral Temple (太庙), where emperors honoured their ancestors. West of the axis: the Altar of Land and Grain (社稷坛), for the gods of the soil and the crops. Seen by the emperor facing south, the temple is on his left and the altar on his right. Today they are the Working People’s Cultural Palace and Zhongshan Park.

clips.send: Summer Palace. Today: Haidian, Beijing. A huge royal garden with Longevity Hill and Kunming Lake. Its Long Corridor is painted with more than 14,000 pictures.
clips.text: Summer Palace. Today: Haidian, Beijing. A huge royal garden with Longevity Hill and Kunming Lake. Its Long Corridor is painted with more than 14,000 pictures.

clips.send: West wing (西厢房). Faces east. More bedrooms for the younger generation. It gets the morning sun.
clips.text: West wing (西厢房)。 Faces east。 More bedrooms for the younger generation.。 It gets the morning sun.

clips.send: Courtyard (院子). The family’s outdoor living room. All the rooms open onto the yard, not onto the street: quiet, safe and sunny. Families planted trees such as jujube and crabapple, raised goldfish and sat out on summer evenings.

clips.send: South row (倒座房). Faces north, toward the yard. Its back wall is on the hutong, and its windows face north into the front yard. It gets the least sun, so it was used for guests, servants, storage or a study.

clips.send: Olympic Park. The “Bird’s Nest” stadium and the “Water Cube” stand on either side of the Central Axis. Beijing is the first city to host both Summer (2008) and Winter (2022) Olympics.

clips.send: Great Hall of the People. Today: West side of Tian’anmen Square, Beijing. The National People’s Congress meets here. Its main auditorium seats about 10,000 people.

clips.send: Drum Tower and Bell Tower. Drums sounded the hours at night and the bell rang at dawn. The bronze bell in the Bell Tower weighs about 63 tonnes.

clips.send: Bell Tower. The northern end of the axis. Rebuilt in 1745–1747 (Qing) entirely of brick and stone, so it could not burn down again. About 48 m (157 ft) tall. Its bronze bell, cast in the Ming Yongle years, weighs about 63 t: as much as five school buses. You have walked about 7.8 km, about 4.8 miles!

clips.send: Altar of Land and Grain. Today: Zhongshan Park, Beijing. The square altar is covered with soil of five colours, standing for the east, south, west, north and centre of the land.

clips.send: Tian’anmen Square. One of the largest city squares in the world. About 44 hectares: roughly 80 US football fields. A national flag-raising ceremony is held here at sunrise every day. On the axis: the Monument to the People’s Heroes (completed 1958). On the sides: the Great Hall of the People (west), where the National People’s Congress meets, and the National Museum of China (east).

clips.send: Hutong (胡同). The lane outside. Old Beijing’s lanes. Most of them run east–west, so the courtyard houses between them can all face south. Many hutongs date back to the Yuan dynasty; one popular theory says the word comes from a Mongolian word for “well”.

clips.send: Yongdingmen Gate. The southern start of the axis. Built in 1553 (Ming dynasty) as the main south gate of the new outer city. The name means “Gate of Lasting Peace”. Torn down in 1957 to make room for traffic, then rebuilt in 2004 from old drawings and photos. From here the axis runs dead straight north for about 7.8 km (4.8 mi).

clips.send: 故宫（紫禁城）。 明清两代 24 位皇帝的皇宫。 1406—1420 年建成，南北长约 961 米，东西宽约 753 米（约 72 公顷），四周有 10 米高的城墙和宽阔的护城河。 约有 8700 间房屋；中轴线上的太和殿是我国现存最大的木结构大殿。 从南面的午门进入，从北面的神武门出来。1925 年成立故宫博物院，1987 年列入《世界遗产名录》。

clips.send: 先农坛。 中轴线西侧。 建于 1420 年。每年春天，皇帝到这里亲自耕田，表示重视农业。 它位于中轴线西侧，和东侧的天坛相对称。 现在这里是北京古代建筑博物馆。

clips.send: 天安门广场。 世界上最大的城市广场之一。 面积约 44 公顷，大约相当于 80 个美式橄榄球场。 每天日出时在这里举行升国旗仪式。 中轴线上有人民英雄纪念碑（1958 年建成）；西侧是全国人民代表大会开会的人民大会堂，东侧是中国国家博物馆。

clips.send: 永定门。 中轴线的南起点。 建于明代 1553 年，是外城的正南门，“永定”意为永远安定。 1957 年因交通需要被拆除，2004 年依据老图纸和照片复建。 从这里，中轴线笔直向北延伸约 7.8 千米。

clips.send: 万宁桥。 中轴线上最古老的桥（1285 年）。 始建于元代 1285 年，至今仍在通行。 元代时，京杭大运河的漕船从桥下驶入积水潭（今什刹海），这里是大运河的北端终点。 桥两岸雕有镇水兽。

clips.send: 太庙与社稷坛。 左祖右社。 中轴线东侧是太庙，皇帝在这里祭祀祖先。 中轴线西侧是社稷坛，祭祀土地神和五谷神。 皇帝坐北朝南，太庙在左、社稷坛在右，这就是“左祖右社”。今天它们分别是劳动人民文化宫和中山公园。

clips.text: 大门。 开在东南角。 大门开在角上，而不是正中，加上门内的影壁，胡同里的人看不到院子里面，保护了隐私。。 也能挡住从街上吹进来的风沙。

clips.send: 天安门。1949年10月1日，毛泽东主席在天安门城楼上宣告中华人民共和国中央人民政府成立。城楼前的广场能容纳约一百万人。
